title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1RC0RE_1RD0RA_1RE1LC_0LA0RF_1LE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1RC0RE_1RD0RA_1RE1LC_0LA0RF_1LE---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves two crossings of the sweeps and the situations that lead to a halt (kernel), and no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in 109 steps.

What it does. The mirror image of a known family: at the right end the tape is dense, blocks of 1s of length 4j+3 separated by single 0s; at the left end it is sparse, the words 01, 0001 and 00. The sweeps translate between the two forms; going left, E with a 0 ahead turns each 11 into 10. The list of block lengths is scrambled on every trip.
Where a halt would come from. Only F reading a 1 halts; E>1 1, 1 F>0, B>1 1 1 and D>0 1 1 lead there. In 2·108 steps F always reads a 0.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: B with 1 under the head, 1 right, 1 two right; D with 0 under the head, 1 right, 1 two right; F with 1 left, 0 under the head. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 35,871 cells have been visited and 23,301 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.504).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: Going left, E with a 0 ahead turns each 11 into 10 (four steps a pair); going right, A turns each 0101 into 1110 (six steps a copy).

claims.title: The halting situations
claims.text: E>1 1 halts after one step; 1 F>0, B>1 1 1 and D>0 1 1 after two.

claims.title: Dense and sparse forms
claims.text: At the 1,804 right-end visits of the first 5·10<sup>6</sup> steps, 273,318 of the 275,315 blocks of 1s strictly inside the tape have length 4j+3; at the 655 left-end visits every 1 stands alone (the sparse words), with 29 exceptions.

claims.title: F never reads a 1 in 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps
claims.text: In the first 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps the machine is in state F 22,449,902 times, every time on a 0: the halting transition F1 is never close to firing in a way the run shows.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 24, history 1 up to width 24, history 2 up to width 24, history 3 up to width 24, LRU history up to width 7 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 20, p = 3 up to width 20, p = 4 up to width 20, p = 6 up to width 20. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..8; n = 9 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The list of block lengths behaves like the content of a cellular automaton; no invariant excluding the halting situations is known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine shuttles its tape between a dense encoding at the right end and a sparse one at the left end, scrambling it a little on every trip. This page runs it in your browser.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 35,871 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Two encodings of one list
html: Look at the tape each time the head turns. At the right end it is dense: blocks of 1s, almost all of length 3, 7, 11, … (4j+3), separated by single 0s. At the left end it is sparse: the words 01, 0001 and 00.
Going left, E (with a 0 ahead) halves each pair of 1s, four steps a pair:
(Lean: left_E.) Going right, A turns each 0101 into 1110 (right_A), which rebuilds the dense blocks. As in its mirror family, the list of block lengths is scrambled on each round trip.

sections.heading: F must read a 1
html: Only F reading a 1 halts. E on a 1 moves right into F, so E reading two 1s halts:
F is entered 22 million times in the first 2·108 steps, always on a 0.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.504).
After 109 steps the tape spans 35,871 cells (6,676 left of the start, 19,755 right), with a density of 1s of 0.65.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0RD_1RC0RE_1RD1LB_0LE0RF_1RA0LD_1LD---: rename A→E, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→F; it is this table started in state B

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

summary: Sweeps between a sparse form (words 01 and 0001) at the left end and a dense form (blocks 1<sup>4j+3</sup> separated by single 0s) at the right end; the list of blocks is scrambled on every round trip. Open.
family: two-sided bouncer, dense/sparse translator with chaotic content
